17	import 'placeholder_screens.dart';
18	
19	/// Every route this app shell resolves — Story 1.6's original set
20	/// (`/boot`, `/auth`, `/reauth`, `/`, `/meus-registros`, `/planos-de-acao`,
21	/// `/configuracoes`) plus Epic 2/spec-2-1's `/vault` lock screen. Named
22	/// constants so no call site retypes a path literal that could drift from
23	/// the one `GoRouter` below.
24	abstract final class AppRoutePaths {
25	  static const boot = '/boot';
26	  static const auth = '/auth';
27	  static const reauth = '/reauth';
28	  static const vaultLock = '/vault';
29	  static const home = '/';
30	  static const meusRegistros = '/meus-registros';
31	  static const planosDeAcao = '/planos-de-acao';
32	  static const configuracoes = '/configuracoes';
33	}
34	
35	/// The epic's ONE `GoRouter`/`redirect` (Boundaries: "never a second
36	/// competing `redirect`") — composes [VaultRepository.currentStatus] first,
37	/// then [SessionRepository.currentStatus] (AD-14). All three repositories
38	/// are taken as parameters (rather than this file reaching into `sl`
39	/// itself) purely so a test can pass fakes/mocks directly, without
40	/// touching the global DI container; `AccountSettingsRepository` (Story
41	/// 2.4) only ever feeds `VaultLockScreen.attemptBiometricFirst` and the
42	/// router's own `refreshListenable` — it plays no part in `_redirect`
43	/// itself.
44	///
45	/// [navigatorKey] is accepted explicitly (rather than letting `GoRouter`
46	/// generate its own internally) so the caller — `main.dart`'s
47	/// `ExpiryOverlayHost` — can reach the Navigator's own `BuildContext`
48	/// through the same, public, documented key instead of reaching into
49	/// `GoRouter`'s internal `routerDelegate` (not part of its public API).
50	GoRouter buildAppRouter({
51	  required VaultRepository vaultRepository,
52	  required SessionRepository sessionRepository,
53	  required AccountSettingsRepository accountSettingsRepository,
54	  required GlobalKey<NavigatorState> navigatorKey,
55	}) {
56	  return GoRouter(
57	    navigatorKey: navigatorKey,
58	    initialLocation: AppRoutePaths.boot,
59	    refreshListenable: _GoRouterRefreshStream([
60	      vaultRepository.statusStream,
61	      sessionRepository.statusStream,
62	      // Story 2.4 — a toggle flipped elsewhere (the Configurações screen
63	      // itself) must re-trigger `/vault`'s own `builder` the next time
64	      // `_redirect` sends the user there, same "re-run on every emission"
65	      // rationale AD-14 already gives the other two streams.
66	      accountSettingsRepository.biometricEnabledStream,
67	    ]),
68	    redirect: (context, state) =>
69	        _redirect(vaultRepository, sessionRepository, state),
70	    routes: [
71	      GoRoute(
72	        path: AppRoutePaths.vaultLock,
73	        builder: (context, state) => VaultLockScreen(
74	          vaultRepository: vaultRepository,
75	          // Story 2.4 — read synchronously, same sync-getter convention
76	          // `_redirect` already uses for `VaultStatus`/`SessionStatus`
77	          // below: `true` (the default before the boot fetch resolves)
78	          // attempts biometric first, `false` skips straight to the PIN
79	          // keypad (Boundaries).
80	          attemptBiometricFirst:
81	              accountSettingsRepository.currentBiometricEnabled,
82	        ),
83	      ),
84	      GoRoute(
85	        path: AppRoutePaths.boot,
86	        builder: (context, state) => const BootSplashScreen(),
87	      ),
88	      GoRoute(
89	        path: AppRoutePaths.auth,
90	        builder: (context, state) => AuthScreen(
91	          cubit: sl<AuthCubit>(),
92	          onAuthenticated: (context) => context.go(AppRoutePaths.home),
93	        ),
94	      ),
95	      GoRoute(
96	        path: AppRoutePaths.reauth,
97	        builder: (context, state) => const BiometricReauthPlaceholderScreen(),
98	      ),
99	      GoRoute(
100	        path: AppRoutePaths.home,
101	        builder: (context, state) => const HomeChatPlaceholderScreen(),
102	      ),
103	      GoRoute(
104	        path: AppRoutePaths.meusRegistros,
105	        builder: (context, state) => const MeusRegistrosPlaceholderScreen(),
106	      ),
107	      GoRoute(
108	        path: AppRoutePaths.planosDeAcao,
109	        builder: (context, state) => const ActionPlansPlaceholderScreen(),
110	      ),
111	      GoRoute(
112	        path: AppRoutePaths.configuracoes,
113	        builder: (context, state) =>
114	            AccountSettingsScreen(cubit: sl<AccountSettingsCubit>()),
115	      ),
116	    ],
117	  );
118	}
119	
120	/// I/O & Edge-Case Matrix:
121	/// - status not yet known (`null`) -> `/boot`, unless already there.
122	/// - `unauthenticated` -> `/auth`, unless already there.
123	/// - `authenticated`/`expired` -> leaves `/boot`/`/auth` for `/`; every
124	///   other location is left alone *except* `/reauth` while already
125	///   `authenticated` (bounced home below — `/reauth` is meant to be
126	///   reached only by the expiry overlay's own explicit navigation while
127	///   `expired`, code review Story 1.6) — a mid-session expiry never
128	///   navigates away (Story 1.5 behavior preserved), and the three
129	///   non-Home destinations stay reachable while `expired`.
130	///
131	/// AD-14: Epic 2's `VaultStatus` gate (RF03) is composed first, strictly
132	/// ahead of every `SessionStatus` check below — the vault gate overrides
133	/// any location whenever it isn't `unlocked`, and only once it is does the
134	/// rest of this function (unchanged from Story 1.6) ever run.
135	String? _redirect(
136	  VaultRepository vaultRepository,
137	  SessionRepository sessionRepository,
138	  GoRouterState state,
139	) {
140	  final location = state.matchedLocation;
141	
142	  // AD-14 — checked before SessionStatus, per Boundaries ("`_redirect`
143	  // checks `VaultStatus` before `SessionStatus`"). `VaultStatus.locked` is
144	  // the default from construction (never `null`), so this never waits on
145	  // an async warm-up the way the `status == null` boot check below does.
146	  if (vaultRepository.currentStatus != VaultStatus.unlocked) {
147	    return location == AppRoutePaths.vaultLock
148	        ? null
149	        : AppRoutePaths.vaultLock;
150	  }
151	
152	  final status = sessionRepository.currentStatus;
153	
154	  if (status == null) {
155	    return location == AppRoutePaths.boot ? null : AppRoutePaths.boot;
156	  }
157	
158	  if (status == SessionStatus.unauthenticated) {
159	    return location == AppRoutePaths.auth ? null : AppRoutePaths.auth;
160	  }
161	
162	  // status is authenticated or expired.
163	  // `vaultLock` is included here too: once the vault unlocks while this
164	  // location is still `/vault` (the normal cold-start path once
165	  // `authenticate()` succeeds), the same fall-through that already bounces
166	  // `/boot`/`/auth` to Home applies — `/vault` is never a valid resting
167	  // place once `VaultStatus.unlocked`.
168	  if (location == AppRoutePaths.boot ||
169	      location == AppRoutePaths.auth ||
170	      location == AppRoutePaths.vaultLock) {
171	    return AppRoutePaths.home;
172	  }
173	  // `/reauth` is a throwaway placeholder standing in for Epic 2's real
174	  // reauth flow; it should never be sitting open once the session is back
175	  // to fully `authenticated` (code review, Story 1.6).
176	  if (location == AppRoutePaths.reauth &&
177	      status == SessionStatus.authenticated) {
178	    return AppRoutePaths.home;
179	  }
180	  return null;
181	}
182	
183	/// Wraps [streams] as a single `Listenable` so `GoRouter`'s
184	/// `refreshListenable` can re-run [_redirect] on every emission from either
185	/// one — go_router 18.1.1 exports no `GoRouterRefreshStream` of its own
186	/// (Code Map), so this is that small local class. Extended by AD-14 to
187	/// subscribe to both the vault and the session streams (previously just
188	/// the one session stream), composing them into the one `Listenable`
189	/// `GoRouter` itself requires (Boundaries: "never a second
190	/// `GoRouter`/`redirect`").
191	class _GoRouterRefreshStream extends ChangeNotifier {
192	  _GoRouterRefreshStream(Iterable<Stream<dynamic>> streams) {
193	    _subscriptions = [
194	      for (final stream in streams)
195	        stream.listen(
196	          (_) => notifyListeners(),
197	          // Mirrors `ExpiryOverlayHost`'s and `SessionRepositoryImpl`'s own
198	          // subscriptions to this same stream — no current implementation
199	          // ever errors on it, but a future one that did must not surface
200	          // as an unhandled zone exception here specifically.
201	          onError: (_, _) {},
202	        ),
203	    ];
204	  }
205	
206	  late final List<StreamSubscription<dynamic>> _subscriptions;
207	
208	  @override
209	  void dispose() {
210	    for (final subscription in _subscriptions) {
211	      subscription.cancel();
212	    }
213	    super.dispose();
214	  }
215	}

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

Spec-2.4 (biometric preference persistence) implementation verified and completed.

## Status found at start
Nearly the entire implementation already existed in the working tree as uncommitted changes (likely from a prior session): `AccountSettingsRepository`/`AccountSettingsRepositoryImpl`/`AccountRemoteDataSource`/`AccountSettingsDto`, `AccountSettingsCubit`/`AccountSettingsState`, `AccountSettingsScreen`, `BackArrowHeader` extraction, `registerAccountFeature()`, and all the wiring in `injection_container.dart`, `app_router.dart`, `main.dart`, `vault_lock_screen.dart`, `placeholder_screens.dart` — all exactly matching the spec's Code Map. Tests existed for the data source, repository impl, and cubit, but **no test existed for `AccountSettingsScreen`** (the one gap against the Code Map's "tests for every file").

## What I changed

1. **Added `test/features/account/presentation/screens/account_settings_screen_test.dart`** (new, 6 tests) — covers the Acceptance Criteria directly against the real widget: header/title/switch-only rendering, switch mirrors `currentBiometricEnabled` at construction (both true and false), tap-to-toggle success (flip, no error band), tap-to-toggle failure (revert + `Failure.message` shown inline), and the shared back-arrow navigation.

2. **Fixed 2 pre-existing failing tests in `test/features/account/presentation/cubit/account_settings_cubit_test.dart`**:
   - `_emittedDuring()` now drains with `pumpEventQueue()` instead of a single `Future.delayed(Duration.zero)` — the `biometricEnabled` mirror travels repository → `Stream.multi`'s forwarding subscription → cubit's `emit()`, several microtask hops deep; one delay only drains one hop.
   - The "switch reverts" test's assertion was over-specified: it pinned an exact emission order between two independently-timed paths (the stream-mirrored flip/revert vs. the cubit's own direct `errorMessage` emit) whose relative order isn't guaranteed by either's contract. Relaxed to assert what the I/O matrix actually requires — `false` was visible at some point, and the settled end state is `{true, 'Sem conexão'}` — rather than a brittle exact sequence.
   - The "later successful toggle" test needed a `pumpEventQueue()` drain before asserting `cubit.state`, for the same reason.

3. **No `lib/` production code was changed** — everything needed already matched the spec exactly (verified `AccountSettingsCubit`, `AccountSettingsRepositoryImpl`, `AccountRemoteDataSource`, `AccountSettingsScreen`, `vault_lock_screen.dart`'s `attemptBiometricFirst` gating, `app_router.dart`'s `/vault` and `/configuracoes` wiring, and `main.dart`'s boot-time `fetchBiometricEnabled()` call line by line against the Boundaries/I-O matrix — all correct).

## A genuine environment finding worth flagging

While building the new screen test, I hit a real, reproducible gotcha: constructing a `Cubit` (with a `StreamSubscription` set up in its own constructor) inside `package:test`'s `setUp()` and then driving it through `testWidgets`/`tester.pump()` left the widget permanently stuck on stale state — `cubit.state` updated correctly, but `BlocBuilder` never rebuilt, no matter how many pumps (even 50) or how `pumpEventQueue()` was used (which, note, hangs forever under `TestWidgetsFlutterBinding`'s fake-async zone — it schedules via `Timer`, not microtasks). Isolated via bisection to the `setUp()`/`late` pattern specifically: `setUp()` callbacks run in `package:test`'s outer per-test zone, a different zone than the one `TestWidgetsFlutterBinding` establishes for the `testWidgets` body itself, and a subscription created in the outer zone doesn't get its events reliably flushed by `tester.pump()`. Fix: construct the cubit/repository fake *inside* the `testWidgets` callback (a `_pumpScreen` helper), not via `setUp()`. Documented this in the test file's doc comments. This is worth knowing if anyone else writes a `testWidgets` test for a Cubit with its own internal stream subscription in this codebase.

## Verification run

- `fvm flutter pub get` — resolved clean.
- `fvm flutter pub run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs` — 0 outputs written (all generated code already current).
- `fvm flutter analyze` — **No issues found!**
- `fvm flutter test` — **All 358 tests passed** (full suite, run twice to confirm, plus the new/fixed account files re-run 3x individually for stability — no flakiness observed).

## Files touched by me
- `/Users/wagnerduarte/Documents/Faculdade/2026.2/TCC/cerne-ciclo-b/test/features/account/presentation/screens/account_settings_screen_test.dart` (new)
- `/Users/wagnerduarte/Documents/Faculdade/2026.2/TCC/cerne-ciclo-b/test/features/account/presentation/cubit/account_settings_cubit_test.dart` (fixed 2 failing tests)

Everything else relevant to spec-2-4 (listed in the spec's Code Map) was already present and correct in the working tree; I verified each file against the spec's Boundaries, I/O matrix, and Acceptance Criteria rather than re-writing working code.

## Nothing left incomplete
All five I/O-matrix rows are covered across the repository/cubit/screen/vault-lock-screen/router/main test layers. No `lib/` files remain to be written. No `docs/input/` files were touched. No extension features were implemented. The `_bmad-output/` and other unrelated modified files (vault idle-timeout review fixes, pin_keypad changes, deferred-work.md, sprint-status.yaml) were already present in the working tree before I started and are outside spec-2-4's scope — I left them untouched.

The coordinator sent a message while you were working:
Three review passes (blind-hunter, edge-case-hunter, verification-gap) ran against the diff for spec-2-4-biometric-preference-persistence.md, which you just implemented. After triage, these 7 findings are classified as real, caused by this story, and trivially fixable without changing the frozen spec — please apply all of them now, then re-run `fvm flutter analyze` and `fvm flutter test` and confirm both are still clean.

1. **`lib/features/account/account_injection.dart`** — `AccountSettingsCubit`'s registration has no `dispose:` callback, unlike `AccountSettingsRepository`/`VaultRepository`/`SessionRepository` right next to it in the same file. `AccountSettingsCubit`'s constructor subscribes to `biometricEnabledStream` and only cancels that subscription in its own `close()`, which nothing currently calls. Fix: add `dispose: (cubit) => cubit.close()` to the `AccountSettingsCubit` registration, matching the existing convention.

2. **`lib/features/account/data/repositories/account_settings_repository_impl.dart`** (+ cubit/screen) — `setBiometricEnabled()` has no in-flight guard: two overlapping toggles (double-tap), or a boot `fetchBiometricEnabled()` resolving while a `setBiometricEnabled()` call is still in flight, let a stale call's revert/emit stomp a newer one's already-confirmed value. `vault_repository_impl.dart` already solves this exact class of bug with a generation counter (`_submitPinGeneration`) and `vault_lock_screen.dart` disables its UI while a call is pending (`_submittingPin`). Fix: add an equivalent generation/sequence counter in `AccountSettingsRepositoryImpl` covering both `fetchBiometricEnabled()` and `setBiometricEnabled()` so only the latest call's result is ever applied, and disable the `Switch` in `account_settings_screen.dart` while a toggle is in flight (expose an `isSaving`-style flag on `AccountSettingsState`/the cubit) so a user can't trigger the race via double-tap in the first place.

3. **`lib/features/account/presentation/cubit/account_settings_cubit.dart`** — `AccountSettingsState.errorMessage` is only cleared at the start of the *next* `toggleBiometric()` call. Because `AccountSettingsCubit` is a `registerLazySingleton` (one instance for the app's lifetime), a failed toggle's error text is still showing if the user leaves "Configurações" and returns later with no new attempt made. This is the exact same "stale message lingers unchanged" bug this diff already fixed for `vault_lock_screen.dart`'s PIN-mismatch error — apply the same fix here: clear `errorMessage` when the Configurações screen is (re)entered, not only when a fresh toggle starts. (`AccountSettingsScreen` is currently `StatelessWidget` wrapping `BlocProvider.value`; the simplest fix is likely converting it to clear the cubit's error on mount, or having the cubit itself not persist a stale error past the screen's own lifecycle — use your judgment on the minimal change.)

4. **`lib/features/vault/presentation/screens/vault_lock_screen.dart`** — `attemptBiometricFirst` is only consulted once, in `initState()`. If `/vault` rebuilds while `VaultLockScreen` is already mounted (same widget type, no key) and `attemptBiometricFirst` has changed since mount — e.g. the boot-time `fetchBiometricEnabled()` resolves to `false` just after the vault screen already mounted and auto-attempted biometric — the change is silently ignored until the screen remounts, even though `app_router.dart`'s own doc comment states the `biometricEnabledStream`-in-`refreshListenable` wiring exists specifically to make this reactive. Fix: add a `didUpdateWidget` override that re-applies the same `attemptBiometricFirst`-true/false branching from `initState` whenever the value changes from `false`→state-not-yet-on-keypad, or at minimum keeps the screen's behavior consistent with the latest value — use your judgment on the exact mechanics given the existing `_showPinKeypad`/`_attemptAuthenticate` state machine, but the end result must be that a value change reaching an already-mounted `VaultLockScreen` is actually honored, not silently dropped.

5. **`test/core/di/bootstrap_integration_test.dart`** — this file has an established per-feature pattern: "setupCoreDependencies also wires the auth feature" and "...the vault feature" tests, each resolving the real registered type through `sl` to catch a broken registration/dependency cycle. No equivalent "...wires the account feature" test was added for this story. Fix: add one, mirroring the vault one's shape exactly — assert `sl.isRegistered<AccountSettingsRepository>()`/`<AccountSettingsCubit>()` and that `sl<AccountSettingsCubit>()` (or `sl<AccountSettingsRepository>()`) resolves without throwing.

6. **`test/features/account/data/repositories/account_settings_repository_impl_test.dart`** — the `dispose()` test group only proves `fetchBiometricEnabled()` is a silent no-op after disposal; it never calls `setBiometricEnabled()` after `dispose()`, which exercises the same closed-controller guard from the optimistic-flip side. Add that case.

7. **`test/core/navigation/app_router_test.dart`** — the three "Story 2.4" tests in the `AccountSettingsRepository feeds /vault and /configuracoes` group only ever read `currentBiometricEnabled` at the moment the router/screen first builds; none of them calls `fakeAccountSettingsRepository.setValue(...)` *after* the router is already built and asserts any resulting change — so nothing currently proves the `biometricEnabledStream` → `refreshListenable` wiring (finding #4 above) actually does anything. Once #4 is fixed, add a test that emits a new value after building, drives `/vault` to rebuild (or whatever is needed given your #4 fix), and asserts the new value is honored.

Please apply all 7, then run `fvm flutter analyze` and `fvm flutter test`, and report back: what you changed per item, and the verification output (pass/fail counts). If any single item turns out to need a design decision beyond a mechanical fix, flag that one specifically rather than guessing — but items 1, 5, and 6 should be entirely mechanical.

Address this before completing your current task.

input.message:
Applied 6 of the 7 review findings as mechanical/design fixes; flagging #4/#7 together because the shared premise behind them doesn't hold for this go_router version — details below. Both `fvm flutter analyze` and `fvm flutter test` are clean.

## Verification
- `fvm flutter analyze` — **No issues found!**
- `fvm flutter test` — **All 366 tests passed** (358 baseline + 8 new: 1 DI test, 2 repository generation-guard tests, 2 `VaultLockScreen.didUpdateWidget` tests, 2 `AccountSettingsScreen` tests for isSaving/stale-error, 1 repository dispose test).

## What I changed, per finding

**1. `lib/features/account/account_injection.dart`** — added `dispose: (cubit) => cubit.close()` to `AccountSettingsCubit`'s registration. Mechanical, matches the file's existing convention exactly.

**2. `lib/features/account/data/repositories/account_settings_repository_impl.dart`** — added an `int _generation` counter (same pattern as `VaultRepositoryImpl._submitPinGeneration`), incremented at the start of both `fetchBiometricEnabled()` and `setBiometricEnabled()`. Each call captures its own generation; a result is only applied if the captured generation still matches the field when the PATCH resolves — otherwise it's discarded (a superseded `setBiometricEnabled()` returns `Left(Failure.malformedResponse('Superseded by a newer preference update'))`). Added `isSaving` to `AccountSettingsState` (`lib/features/account/presentation/cubit/account_settings_cubit.dart`) — `toggleBiometric()` sets it `true` at start, `false` on either outcome. `account_settings_screen.dart`'s `Switch.onChanged` is now `null` while `state.isSaving`, so a double-tap can never even start a second overlapping call (the generation guard is the backstop for the other race — a boot fetch overlapping a toggle — which the UI can't prevent). New tests: two repository-level race tests (stale fetch vs. newer toggle; older overlapping toggle vs. newer one) in `account_settings_repository_impl_test.dart`, and one screen-level test proving the Switch disables itself mid-flight.

**3. `lib/features/account/presentation/cubit/account_settings_cubit.dart`** — added `clearStaleError()` (clears `errorMessage` only if set). `account_settings_screen.dart` is now a `StatefulWidget`; `initState()` calls `widget.cubit.clearStaleError()`. Since `GoRoute.builder` constructs a fresh `AccountSettingsScreen` (and thus a fresh `State`, running `initState` again) on every navigation to `/configuracoes`, a stale error from a previous visit is cleared on re-entry without touching the cubit's singleton lifetime. New test added proving a stale error is gone after a simulated re-entry (new screen instance, same cubit).

**5. `test/core/di/bootstrap_integration_test.dart`** — added the "wires the account feature" test, mirroring the vault one's shape exactly (asserts `isRegistered<AccountSettingsRepository>()`/`<AccountSettingsCubit>()`, forces resolution via `sl<AccountSettingsCubit>()`).

**6. `test/features/account/data/repositories/account_settings_repository_impl_test.dart`** — added the `setBiometricEnabled()`-after-`dispose()` case to the `dispose()` group, exercising the optimistic-flip side of the closed-controller guard.

## Flagging #4 + #7 together — a design decision, not a mechanical fix

I did apply #4's literal ask: `VaultLockScreen` now has a `didUpdateWidget` that, when `attemptBiometricFirst` flips `true` → `false` while still on the biometric view (not yet on the keypad), proactively switches to the PIN keypad — same effect as the user tapping "Usar PIN". This is correctly implemented and **directly unit-tested** in `vault_lock_screen_test.dart` (two new tests: the true→false switch, and confirming false→true deliberately does *not* retroactively re-trigger biometric on a user already on the keypad) — both pass.

Where I had to stop and flag: #7 asked me to prove this end-to-end through `app_router_test.dart` — that `biometricEnabledStream` in `refreshListenable` actually causes `/vault`'s mounted screen to rebuild with a new value while the user is sitting on it. I wrote that test and it **failed**: empirically, go_router 18.1.1's `GoRouterDelegate.setNewRoutePath` short-circuits (`if (currentConfiguration == configuration) return;`) whenever the redirect's resulting `RouteMatchList` is unchanged — which it always is here, since `_redirect` returns `null` (stay at `/vault`) both before and after the account-settings value changes. The route's `builder` closure (which reads `accountSettingsRepository.currentBiometricEnabled` fresh) is therefore **never re-invoked** while already resident at `/vault`; I confirmed this directly by instrumenting the test and reading `VaultLockScreen.attemptBiometricFirst` across 5 pumps after flipping the value — it never changed from its initial-mount value. This contradicts the existing doc comment in `app_router.dart` (and the finding's own premise) that this wiring makes an already-mounted `/vault` reactive.

So: my `didUpdateWidget` fix is real and correct for *any* future rebuild of `VaultLockScreen` (e.g. if something else in the tree causes one), but the specific router-level path #7 asked me to prove doesn't exist with the current wiring — testing it honestly would mean asserting "nothing happens," which doesn't match what #7 asked for. Making the fake test "pass" would require either changing `app_router.dart`'s redirect/route-matching strategy to force a rebuild (e.g., folding the biometric value into the route's path/key so route-match equality fails on change) or calling something like `router.refresh()` explicitly from the stream listener — both are real design choices about how aggressively to force go_router rebuilds, not a one-line fix, and I didn't want to guess at that unilaterally. I reverted my `app_router_test.dart` additions (the `authenticateGate` field and the failing test) back to the pre-existing state rather than leave a dishonest assertion in place. **This one needs your call**: is the router-level reactivity worth the design change, or is `VaultLockScreen`'s own defensive `didUpdateWidget` (which fires correctly whenever the widget *is* rebuilt by any means) sufficient for spec-2-4's actual scope, given the frozen spec's I/O matrix never explicitly requires live-updating an already-mounted `/vault`?

## Files touched in this pass
- `lib/features/account/account_injection.dart`
- `lib/features/account/data/repositories/account_settings_repository_impl.dart`
- `lib/features/account/presentation/cubit/account_settings_cubit.dart`
- `lib/features/account/presentation/screens/account_settings_screen.dart`
- `lib/features/vault/presentation/screens/vault_lock_screen.dart`
- `test/core/di/bootstrap_integration_test.dart`
- `test/features/account/data/repositories/account_settings_repository_impl_test.dart`
- `test/features/account/presentation/screens/account_settings_screen_test.dart`
- `test/features/vault/presentation/screens/vault_lock_screen_test.dart`
- `test/core/navigation/app_router_test.dart` (touched then reverted to its pre-existing state — net no-op, left as a record in case useful)

message.content:
The coordinator sent a message while you were working:
Good work surfacing that, and good call not faking a passing test. Here's the decision on #4/#7:

**Keep** the `didUpdateWidget` defensive fix in `vault_lock_screen.dart` — it's correct, cheap, tested, and real future-proofing if anything else ever rebuilds that widget.

**Don't** pursue a router-level forced-rebuild (`router.refresh()`, folding the value into route identity, etc.). Reasoning: `currentBiometricEnabled` is already read synchronously at `/vault`'s build time, so every *fresh* navigation into `/vault` (triggered by the Vault/Session streams, as already happens today) already picks up the latest value correctly — the stream's inclusion in `refreshListenable` was only ever meant to cover "value changes while already resident at /vault," which you've now shown go_router 18.1.1 never rebuilds for anyway. That's a one-time, benign race (at most one extra biometric prompt on a slow-network cold boot, never a security or dead-end issue — PIN fallback is untouched) that the frozen spec's I/O matrix never promised to cover, and there's no clean way to interrupt an in-flight native biometric dialog regardless. Not worth the new complexity.

Given that, the `accountSettingsRepository.biometricEnabledStream` entry in `app_router.dart`'s `_GoRouterRefreshStream` list is dead code with a doc comment that overclaims what it does. Please:

1. Remove `accountSettingsRepository.biometricEnabledStream` from the `_GoRouterRefreshStream([...])` list in `buildAppRouter` (`lib/core/navigation/app_router.dart`).
2. Fix the doc comment above it (and the one above `buildAppRouter` mentioning "it plays no part in `_redirect` itself") so it no longer claims this stream re-triggers `/vault`'s builder — state plainly that `currentBiometricEnabled` is read synchronously at build time (same convention as `VaultStatus`/`SessionStatus` below it), and that `AccountSettingsRepository` therefore needs no `refreshListenable` entry of its own; the Configurações screen gets its own reactivity directly from the cubit's independent subscription to `biometricEnabledStream`, unrelated to routing.
3. `accountSettingsRepository` stays a required param on `buildAppRouter` (still needed to read `currentBiometricEnabled` and to resolve `sl<AccountSettingsCubit>()`'s dependency chain) — only the dead stream-subscription line and the inaccurate comment go.
4. Re-run `fvm flutter analyze` and `fvm flutter test` and confirm both are still clean, then give me a one-line confirmation.

No test changes should be needed for this (nothing was asserting the removed behavior), but if `flutter test` disagrees, tell me exactly what broke rather than papering over it.

Address this before completing your current task.
